title: Centralize canvas views in the View menu
summary: Centralize canvas display commands in the desktop View menu and a phone-and-tablet Menu tab while removing redundant toggles from beside the zoom controls.

questions.question: Does the current View menu already share state with the canvas display controls?
questions.answer: Pixel grid and Onion skin share editor state, while Live view is a page-level useState and Transparency checkerboard is editor state not currently exposed by the menu.
questions.decision: Menu actions must use the existing shared state keys so checkmarks, keyboard shortcuts, the canvas, and Live Preview panel remain synchronized.

questions.question: Does this work depend on another unfinished specification?
questions.answer: No pending specifications exist; the relevant controls were delivered in existing workspace commits.
questions.decision: Record no spec dependency and treat the existing editor and title-bar contracts as code dependencies.

questions.question: Which display controls should be removed from beside the zoom controls?
questions.answer: All four: Onion skin, Live view, Pixel grid, and Transparency checkerboard.
questions.decision: Leave only fit and zoom controls in the canvas zoom toolbar; move all visible display-mode access into platform menus.

questions.question: How should phone and tablet users access application menus when the desktop title bar is hidden?
questions.answer: Add a Menu dropdown before Home in the bottom tab pane, with File, Edit, View, and Help as categories containing their equivalent child items.
questions.decision: Add a touch-oriented nested Menu tab on phone and tablet, mirror desktop menu actions and availability, and keep it hidden on desktop.

questions.question: Should keyboard shortcuts remain after removing the canvas display buttons?
questions.decision: Preserve O, V, G, and Shift+G and keep their effects synchronized with menu check states.

questions.question: How should display actions behave while the Home tab is active?
questions.decision: Show the View children consistently but disable canvas-specific actions whenever no editor workspace is active, without resetting state.

risks: Duplicating desktop and touch command handlers could make labels, disabled states, or outcomes diverge over time.
Removing the four canvas buttons before the mobile menu is reachable could strand touch users without display controls.
A bottom-anchored nested menu could overflow narrow, landscape, safe-area, or on-screen-keyboard viewports or obscure document tabs.
View commands could mutate presentation while Home is active or accidentally dirty project history.
Refactoring title-bar menu ownership could regress global shortcuts, About focus restoration, outside-click dismissal, or native window commands.
The new Menu tab consumes scarce horizontal space and could reduce access to document tabs on narrow phones.
validation: Add desktop Playwright coverage for all four View menu checkbox states, Home disabling, shortcut synchronization, and the zoom-only toolbar.
Add phone and tablet Playwright coverage for Menu placement before Home, nested File/Edit/View/Help behavior, touch toggles, disabled Home actions, dismissal, and absence of canvas display buttons.
Capture and inspect updated desktop, phone, and tablet snapshots for menu overflow, tab compression, safe-area placement, focus, and canvas space.
Run studio lint, type checking, unit tests, focused Playwright tests, production build, spec validation, formatting checks on touched files, and git diff checks.
Manually verify that view changes do not increment editor dirty state and that unsupported mobile actions preserve their existing safe behavior.
